title: Segmental rotation at 4 Nm of intact T12-S1 columns (text values)

quantity.name: ROM
quantity.definition: segmental rotation at 4.0 Nm from unloaded position, one direction; mean ± SD (only the extreme values stated in the text; all other level/direction values are in the curve test)

source.authors: Guan Y, Yoganandan N, Moore J, Pintar FA, Zhang J, Maiman DJ, Laud P
source.sample: human cadaver T12-S1 lumbosacral columns, radiographically normal for age

protocol.summary: Quasi-static pure moments (force couple on superior vertebra T12) to 4.0 Nm in flexion, extension, right and left lateral bending; S1 end on a 6-axis load cell; 30 s relaxation before each measurement; no preload; no axial rotation tested; off-axis moments monitored (<=0.03 Nm). Per-level rotation from optoelectronic markers.
how_to_simulate: Model T12-S1 ligamentous column; fix S1 (embedded in PMMA), apply pure moment to T12 (embedded), no preload
Apply flexion, extension, right and left lateral bending moments stepwise to 4.0 Nm (static; steps 0.5,1.5,2.5,3.5,4.0 Nm per methods, figure plots 0.5 Nm steps)
Report the rotation of each segment (L1-L2 ... L5-S1) in the loading plane, measured from the unloaded position, at each step
Compare segmental rotation at 4.0 Nm with mean ± SD (one direction, not range)
protocol.notes: Rotation measured from the unloaded neutral position at each moment step (no cycles; not a peak-to-peak range). NZ not reported. Specimens are T12-S1 but data are per-level L1-L2..L5-S1.

extraction.check_notes: Re-read abstract and Results: 7.37±3.69, 4.62±2.56, 4.04±1.11, 2.42±0.90, 1.58±0.63, 2.50±0.75 match.
